name: Vitu
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand sources agree (1 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts
catalog_citation: van den Berg, René & Peter Bachet. 2006. Vitu Grammar Sketch. Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages, vol. 51. Ukarumpa: Summer Institute of Linguistics (SIL-PNG). 258 pp. PDF via web.archive.org/web/20170810011536/http://www-01.sil.org/pacific/png/pubs/92…
catalog_locator: sect. 2.3 Stress, pp. 10-11 (also sect. 2.4 p. 12 syllable patterns; sect. 4 p. 71 on suffix-induced stress shift)
catalog_quote: Stress regularly occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word, such that each vowel counts as a separate syllable. Stressed syllables seem to have a distinctly longer vowel, but this has not been measured acoustically. Notice in the following examples the stress shift when the root is suffixed: 'mata ‘eye’ ma'tagu ‘my eye’ ... 'tangi ‘to cry’ tangi'zia ‘to cry for’ The only case where stress appears to occur on the last syllable is when the second person possessive suffix occurs. ... Phonologically the addition of the suffix creates an extra syllable which is responsible for the shift in stress. ... If the penultimate vowel is high and the antepenultimate vowel is lower and there is no intervening consonant, the stress may shift to the antepenult. This is the case with sequences of au, ai, ou and oi ... 'rauna ‘its leaves’ 'kaua ‘dog’ lo'hoia ‘think’ 'paido ‘coconut’ vu'roua ‘mourning…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation and all three locators (sect. 2.3 pp. 10-11, sect. 2.4 p. 12, p. 71) are verbatim in the PDF we hold/text of van den Berg & Bachet 2006. Deciding source: a 248-page modern descriptive grammar by resident fieldworkers, the top (and only) grammar in Glottolog's list; web search (SIL PNG archive, OLAC, Wikipedia refs, general search for prosody/JIPA/dissertations) found no later phonology or instrumental study of Vitu. The one additional open primary source, the SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (Bachet 1992, rechecked by van den Berg & Ereliu 2006), was downloaded to and states 'Stress is on the penultimate syllable' with V/CV-only syllables, confirming the classification (penultimate, vowel-counting, weight-insensitive; exceptions = au/ai/ou/oi antepenult shift, 2sg -V forms phonetically final-long, a few loans). sources.quote: 'Stress is on the penultimate syllable.' Syllable patterns V and CV only (kau.a 'dog' syllabified as three syllables, consistent with the grammar's vowel-counting rule); CVC only from word-medial vowel elision (var.ti.hi).

sources.note: Only other published sketch covering Vitu phonology; the held grammar (p. 11) cites Ross 2002:363 for treating au/ai/ou/oi as single-syllable diphthongs in Bali, which bears on whether the 'kaua-type antepenult cases are exceptions or regular penult stress under a diphthong analysis. Would not change the penult coding.
